seo.description: 404 page reference for an AI or SaaS product — #01010C base, glass panels, 200ms transitions and #0D214E accent. Copy the prompt or open it staged in Studio.

tagline: “This page seems to have” — the whole 404 page is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: 404 page reference for an AI or SaaS product — #01010C base, glass panels, 200ms transitions and #0D214E accent.
about: 404 Planet gives an AI or SaaS product a finished first screen and the numbers that produced it. The headline reads “This page seems to have”, and the rest of the 404 page is arranged around it. The palette runs deep blue #01010C underneath, muted teal #D1ECF4 for the type and blue #0D214E carrying the accents, and the type is Helvetica, Arial. The reference is built with React and Tailwind CSS, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion is limited to 200ms transitions. Treat it as the brief for an AI or SaaS product 404 page that has to hold up under a rebuild, not just a first look.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: The bar carries the wordmark, the section links and one #0D214E button, measured at type from 80px to 260px and 10px spacing steps so it never grows into a second header. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #0D214E action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: A bar with nothing spare
layout.body: Design the collapsed state before adding a sixth link. The reference was captured at 640x468.

layout.title: Sizes fixed in the brief
layout.body: The list stays short (type from 80px to 260px, 10px spacing steps and 200ms transitions), which is why the whole system can be checked by hand. A rebuild that hits those numbers looks like the reference without further tuning.

layout.title: Numbers where the proof goes
layout.body: Statistics are handled as typography: figures at the display size, labels at the smallest step in the brief, all of it on #0D214E or the ink colour rather than a coloured card. The figures carry the #0D214E accent while everything around them stays on the ink colour.

motion.title: One duration for the controls
motion.body: The timings are short and consistent (200ms), so hover and press states read as one system instead of a set of separate effects. Short timings are why the page reads as authored; a slow default would undo the composition.

motion.title: Pointer states, nothing more
motion.body: The interactive layer is deliberately small: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card. Press states are specified as well as hover, so a tap gives the same confirmation as a click.

fonts.name: Helvetica, Arial
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one stack for the whole page

editorial.title: The numbers behind the 404 page
editorial.body: Type is the first number: type from 80px to 260px and 10px spacing steps. The spacing follows from it, and everything else on the page is positioned against those two values. Nothing in this 404 page depends on a default.

editorial.title: The timing behind the 404 page
editorial.body: A preset animation pack would have been quicker to ship. The brief specifies 200ms transitions and hover and press states instead, which is why the page reads as authored rather than staged. Nothing animates for its own sake in this 404 page.

editorial.title: How the 404 page reflows
editorial.body: The brief describes what changes at each width (the navigation collapses into a mobile menu), which means the mobile version is a decision rather than a squeeze. Contrast is held on the #0D214E accent over the media, and the video is muted and inline. Nothing important is dropped at narrow widths.

faq.question: What does the brief behind 404 Planet actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 7,598 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Do I need React and Tailwind CSS to rebuild 404 Planet?
faq.answer: 404 Planet was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Why is 404 Planet's prompt not printed here?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 7,598-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.
